Compare adult obesity trends across countries and continents

compare_obesity_trend.Rd

Compare one country or area with the rest of its continent, or compare several countries, areas, or continents over a chosen year range.

Usage

compare_obesity_trend(data, comparison_mode, selections, start_year, end_year)

Arguments

data

The cleaned dataset, with entity, region, year, and obesity_pct columns.

comparison_mode

Which view do you want? Choose country_vs_continent (one place versus the rest of its continent), countries (several places), or continents (several continents).

selections

The place(s) or continent(s) to include. Choose one place for country_vs_continent, or 2–5 selections for the other views.

start_year

The first year in your comparison.

end_year

The last year in your comparison.

Value

A tidy table with one row for each year and line, and columns for year, series, and obesity_pct.

Details

For country_vs_continent, the selected place is left out, so “the rest” really means the other places in its continent. In a continent line, every entity gets equal weight, not every person. These are crude estimates, so treat the graph as a conversation starter for a briefing, not a policy report card.

Examples

data(obesity_data)
compare_obesity_trend(
  data = obesity_data,
  comparison_mode = "countries",
  selections = c("India", "Australia"),
  start_year = 1980,
  end_year = 1985
)
#>      year    series obesity_pct
#> 496  1980 Australia   7.5439787
#> 3871 1980     India   0.2782146
#> 497  1981 Australia   7.9656506
#> 3872 1981     India   0.3032421
#> 498  1982 Australia   8.4189000
#> 3873 1982     India   0.3307577
#> 499  1983 Australia   8.9046700
#> 3874 1983     India   0.3609213
#> 500  1984 Australia   9.4176610
#> 3875 1984     India   0.3940604
#> 501  1985 Australia   9.9489520
#> 3876 1985     India   0.4304292
